html:
British forces landed on Hong Kong Island on 26 January 1841, during the First Opium War, and China ceded the island to Britain in the Treaty of Nanking in 1842.

Hong Kong was then a rocky island with a few fishing villages, valued for its deep, sheltered harbour. Britain made it a free port, and merchants who had traded opium and tea at Canton moved in. Kowloon, across the harbour, was added in 1860, and the New Territories were leased in 1898.

The colony grew as a base for trade with China and as a door for emigrants heading to Southeast Asia and America. Banks such as HSBC, founded in 1865, made it a financial centre. British rule lasted until the handover of 1997, apart from the Japanese occupation of 1941 to 1945.
sum: British forces landed on Hong Kong Island on 26 January 1841, during the First Opium War, and China ceded the island to Britain in the Treaty of Nanking in 1842.
